essays.title: Change Within
essays.body:
Of all of the most wicked things on this Earth
There is one thing that we fear the most;
Change
Yet, it is the inevitable
Only guaranteeable

Despite the necessity
Of adaptability
Many find themselves unprepared
Unprepared for what preparedness is for

Change
Is a marvelous thing
It comes in many shapes and sizes
Both massive and small
But all relative
For change is never inconsequential

And I ask myself: why is this so?
Why am I so unready
Change has no method of attack
It comes with no fangs, stingers, or claws
It simply sits,
It’s patient, for it awaits the inevitable

The unprepared, as an adverse effect
Arm change
They give it what they so desperately despise
Change is whatever you mould it to be
But preparedness is a spear

The spear of your goals
Your ambitions
And you mustn’t throw it away
For it is your only weapon
In the chaos of time

essays.title: The History of Stupidity
essays.body:
How good is your eyesight? And your hearing? Good enough to watch and listen to this video, I presume. But define good enough. You don’t need to see every pixel to grasp what you are seeing. But this is only due to a lifetime of neurons developing in the back of your brain, getting better and better at image recognition. The same goes for your hearing – those times when you think you hear your name being called when it wasn’t are examples of your neurons making mistakes, and then correcting themselves in real-time.

That ringing you sometimes randomly get in your ears is called Tinnitus, by the way. And the leading scientific theory as to what the sound actually is coming from is that it’s the sound of the neurons in your brain firing. You see, this usually gets filtered out by a group of neurons dedicated to this task, but sometimes that delicate circuit breaks for whatever reason.

So what is existence? You remember what the ringing it called, right? Tinnitus. And my name is Zachary, by the way. So let’s get this straight: In the last minute, new neurons formed in your brain dedicated to the name of that sound, and if you already knew its name then those neurons were activated again, with new neurons added, strengthening the circuit. And you know that the person who made this video, the person speaking to you right now, is named Zachary. New neurons formed just for that. So am I a part of you now? I mean, I’m literally in your brain. And the more you try to forget me, the harder it’ll be to do so. Despite me being in your brain, I’m not you. But then what are you? Do only some parts of your brain count, and not others? Your brain does a lot of things for you automatically, such as breathing, blinking, swallowing, and sneezing. Do those count towards you? And your brain predetermined your dominant hand, personality, etc. Do you really control yourself? Or is your brain just hardwired to act the way it does because, throughout human history, those who had the most kids had these traits, and simply passed them down to you, making an amalgamation of humanity’s past.

This topic is probably pretty uncomfortable, but why? Why did your brain decide that?
The thing is, we are both human. I understand that you understand this. I know that we are both driven by our desires, hardwired into us. So, let’s talk about it. What do you want to do with your life? Be happy, and find satisfaction with your life? Me too. So how do we do this?

Well, let’s first consider that we all have death sentences. You and I will both die one day, in fact I may be dead depending on how far into the future you’re watching this.
If you found out that nukes were coming and you have twenty minutes left, what would you do? You would try to find peace, right? So we already know what we innately want to do in the final chapter of our life. So let’s just fill in the space between now and the final chapter. As humans, one of our flaws is failing to think of large numbers. It’s hard to plan for when you’re elderly, but you should. My first tip is to open a retirement investment account NOW, and put in as much money as you can. Invest in index funds. Do it today, not later. So in your final chapter you will be rich enough to do the final things you want to do. Now, in the meantime, you should start working out. Stay healthy. Perhaps you can prolong your life and make every year more enjoyable.

In the meantime, you will be operating in society. So you should probably also dedicate some energy to ensuring that this society runs as well as possible.

The purpose of life is to enjoy what you have and every moment. Get the most from everything.

essays.title: Isle Royale
essays.body:
Day 1:
Arrive in Windigo. Set up camp at Washington Creek campground. Enjoy showers and tap water after doing some hikes. Swimming here is also very highly rated.
Set bearings and rest well. Also has a shop and restaurant.
Hikes:
Minong trail.
Washington Creek Trail

Day 2:
Hike to Huginning Cove Campground which is about two miles. Hike along the coast here during the day and enjoy the secluded, teal-colored waters. Again, take showers and get tap water through an easy four mile round trip hike back to Windigo.
Hikes:
East Huginnin Cove Trail. Incorporate this into showering perhaps.
Minong trail.
Bushwacking is possible.
Just swim around or something

Day 3:
Hike two miles back to Windigo with gear and then rent a canoe.
Canoe 4 miles to Grace Island Campground.
Hike around and canoe-explore.
**If the weather prohibits canoeing, head on to Feldtmann lake now and then spend another day at Siskiwit and another day in Windigo.

Day 4:
Spend more time at Grace Island.
Canoe to Agate Beach, 2.8 miles one way, exploring the coast and other islands along the way.
On the route there we can see the shipwreck of SS America.
**If we get stuck at Agate Beach due to sudden inclement weather, we could bushwack back to Windigo but this would require spending the entire day climbing steep ridges and traversing wild valleys, or just set up camp in the restricted area

Day 5:
Return canoe. Hike 9 miles to Feldtmann lake campground via this trail.
Visit Rainbow Cove (U.S. National Park Service) and grace creek overlook

Day 6:
Hike 10 miles to Siskiwit Bay. Should have extremely beautiful views along the way and the campsite should be pristine. More difficult and more elevation change though.

Day 7:
Siskiwit Bay back to Windigo is 11 miles and this video discusses it

Day 8:
Extra day in case it takes longer to hike. Spend this day back in Washington Creek Campground/Windigo if it wasn’t needed.
